desc:
Given two integers n and k, return every way to choose k different numbers from 1..n.

Write each selection as a row in increasing order (so [1,3] is used and [3,1] is not). Rows may be returned in any order.
constraints: The number of selections C(n, k) is at most 5,000
hints: The order inside a selection does not matter, so force an order: write the numbers of a row in increasing order.
Recurse with the smallest number you are still allowed to take. After taking v, the next number must be at least v + 1.
Prune: if the numbers left in start..n cannot fill the remaining slots, there is no point in trying that start value. The loop for the next number can stop at n - (slots still needed) + 1.
editorial: Keep a current row and the next allowed number start. When the row has k numbers, store a copy. Otherwise, for each v from start up to the last value that still leaves enough numbers above it to complete the row, append v, recurse on v + 1, and pop.

The upper bound on v is the pruning that matters: without it the search wastes time on prefixes that can never reach length k. With it every recursive call leads to at least one answer, so the total work is proportional to the output size, C(n, k) · k.
